Hire Resolve is assisting petrochemical organizations in hiring experienced petrochemical professionals to support refinery, chemical, and downstream manufacturing operations across Canada. This is a multi-role opportunity spanning several functions within the sector, including plant operations, process and project engineering, reliability and maintenance, HSE and process safety, quality and laboratory functions, supply chain, and commercial/technical services. These roles are designed for mid- to senior-level professionals and offer a clear progression pathway toward senior leadership roles such as Operations/Production Manager, Engineering Manager, Reliability Lead, HSE/Process Safety Manager, and broader site leadership opportunities.
 Key Responsibilities
 Lead safe, efficient plant operations across continuous and batch processes, utilities, and supporting units 
 Drive process optimization, debottlenecking, yield improvement, energy efficiency, and cost reduction initiatives 
 Support or lead capital projects from scope definition through execution, commissioning, and handover 
 Maintain robust technical documentation and change control (P&IDs, SOPs, operating envelopes, MOC) 
 Strengthen asset reliability through preventive/predictive maintenance strategies, RCA, shutdown/turnaround planning, and integrity programs 
 Ensure compliance with applicable provincial OHS requirements and site HSE management systems, including process safety controls where applicable 
 Lead and participate in risk assessments (PHA/HAZOP/LOPA), incident investigations, and corrective action closeout 
 Manage contractors and safe systems of work (Permit to Work, isolations/LOTO, method statements and risk assessments) 
 Monitor and improve KPIs for safety, production, quality, reliability, and budget performance 
 Collaborate with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Laboratory, Supply Chain, and external vendors to deliver site objectives 
 Support internal and external audits and inspections; maintain continuous improvement initiatives 
 Coach and develop teams through training, competency development, and leadership support
 Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical/Instrumentation Engineering, Chemistry, or a related discipline (a P.Eng. designation or eligibility is an advantage for certain engineering roles) 
 Typically 7–15+ years of experience in petrochemicals, refining, specialty chemicals, polymers, industrial gases, or comparable process manufacturing environments 
 Demonstrated experience in one or more functional tracks: operations leadership, process engineering, reliability/maintenance, rotating equipment, HSE/process safety, projects, quality/laboratory, or commercial/technical support 
 Working knowledge of safety and regulatory expectations in Canada (provincial OHS frameworks, contractor safety, hazardous energy control/LOTO, and process safety practices where applicable) 
 Familiarity with common plant systems and tools such as CMMS/EAM (e.g., SAP/Maximo), process historians (e.g., PI System), and standard engineering documentation practices 
 Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to lead cross-functional teams and drive delivery 
 Willingness to work onsite in an industrial environment; some roles may involve shift coverage, on-call rotation, or travel depending on site needs
 Extended Healthcare Plan (Medical, Disability, Dental & Vision)
 RPP - Group RRSP
 Group Life - AD&D - Critical Illness Insurance
 Paid Time Off Benefits

Présentation de l'entreprise 
 Nous fabriquons et fournissons des médicaments et des vaccins fiables et de haute qualité afin de répondre aux besoins des patients et de soutenir notre performance.
 Notre réseau mondial de production joue un rôle essentiel dans la livraison de produits de santé aux patients partout dans le monde. Grâce à nos technologies de fabrication avancées, à nos solutions numériques et à nos pratiques d'amélioration continue, nous assurons l'excellence opérationnelle, la qualité des produits et la sécurité de nos employés.
 Nous recherchons des leaders inspirants qui souhaitent contribuer à l'innovation, à la performance des procédés et au développement des équipes techniques dans un environnement hautement réglementé et en constante évolution.
 Résumé du poste 
 Le Chef Technologie et Procédé est responsable de la direction stratégique et opérationnelle d'une équipe d'experts techniques soutenant les activités de fabrication de vaccins et d'adjuvants. Il assure la gouvernance technique des procédés, équipements et systèmes sous sa responsabilité tout en veillant à maintenir des opérations sécuritaires, robustes et conformes aux exigences réglementaires.
 À titre de leader, il collabore étroitement avec les équipes de Production, Qualité, Ingénierie, Affaires réglementaires et MSAT Global afin d'orienter les décisions techniques, anticiper les risques et soutenir la performance du site. Il joue un rôle essentiel dans l'amélioration continue des procédés, la gestion du cycle de vie des technologies et le développement des compétences de son équipe.
 Responsabilités 
 Cette fonction vous offrira l'occasion de diriger des activités clés afin de faire progresser votre carrière. Dans le cadre de ce rôle, vous serez notamment appelé(e) à :
 Établir et déployer les orientations stratégiques et opérationnelles de l'équipe en cohérence avec les priorités du site.
 Diriger, mobiliser, développer et évaluer une équipe de professionnels techniques, tout en favorisant leur développement et la planification de la relève.
 Maintenir une gouvernance technique rigoureuse des procédés, équipements, systèmes et technologies sous sa responsabilité.
 Assurer le suivi du cycle de vie des procédés, incluant les stratégies de contrôle, la validation et la vérification continue des procédés.
 Collaborer avec les fonctions partenaires afin d'aligner les priorités, anticiper les risques et faciliter une prise de décision efficace.
 Fournir une expertise technique lors des déviations de production, enquêtes, analyses de causes fondamentales et activités CAPA.
 Diriger les évaluations de risques reliées aux changements de procédés, d'équipements, de systèmes ou de matières.
 Piloter les initiatives d'amélioration continue visant à accroître la robustesse des procédés, la sécurité, la qualité et la performance opérationnelle.
 Utiliser les données et les outils numériques pour soutenir la prise de décision et l'optimisation des procédés.
 Assurer la conformité des activités aux exigences réglementaires, aux BPF et aux standards corporatifs.
 Développer des relations de collaboration fortes avec les intervenants locaux et globaux afin de soutenir les objectifs du site.
 Favoriser un environnement de travail fondé sur la confiance, la responsabilisation, la proactivité et l'innovation.
 Pourquoi vous? 
 Ce poste est offert sur notre site de Sainte-Foy dans un environnement manufacturier hautement réglementé où les activités techniques contribuent directement à la production de vaccins et de produits biologiques complexes.
 Vous aurez l'occasion d'exercer un rôle stratégique ayant un impact important sur la performance des procédés, la conformité réglementaire, le développement des équipes ainsi que la compétitivité du site. Vous intégrerez une organisation qui valorise l'innovation, la collaboration, le développement professionnel et l'amélioration continue.
 Compétences requises 
 Nous recherchons des professionnels possédant les compétences et qualifications suivantes :
 Diplôme universitaire en sciences, en ingénierie ou dans une discipline technique connexe.
 Expérience significative au sein de l'industrie pharmaceutique, biopharmaceutique ou de la fabrication de vaccins.
 Expérience démontrée en gestion de personnel et en développement d'équipes techniques.
 Expérience dans un environnement matriciel et multidisciplinaire.
 Expérience en gestion des risques et en gestion de projets.
 Solide connaissance des Bonnes pratiques de fabrication (BPF) et des exigences réglementaires applicables.
 Excellentes compétences en communication, en influence et en gestion des parties prenantes.
 Capacité démontrée à analyser des situations complexes et à prendre des décisions fondées sur des données scientifiques.
 Excellentes aptitudes en leadership, gestion de la performance et mobilisation d'équipe.
 Maîtrise avancée de l'anglais et capacité à évoluer dans un environnement bilingue.
 Qualifications souhaitées 
 Les qualifications suivantes constitueraient un atout :
 Expérience avec les vaccins, les adjuvants, les produits biologiques ou d'autres procédés stériles complexes.
 Expertise dans des domaines tels que la validation, le contrôle de la contamination, le nettoyage ou l'inspection visuelle.
 Expérience en transfert technologique, validation de procédés ou gestion du cycle de vie technique.
 Expérience dans la direction d'initiatives majeures d'amélioration continue.
 Capacité à synthétiser des informations provenant de plusieurs fonctions et à les traduire en orientations stratégiques claires.
 Connaissance des outils statistiques, analytiques et numériques utilisés pour la surveillance et l'optimisation des procédés.
 Ce que nous offrons 
 Vous aurez l'occasion d'évoluer au sein d'une organisation où la science, l'innovation, la qualité et la sécurité sont au cœur des activités. Vous contribuerez directement à l'évolution des technologies et des procédés de fabrication tout en développant votre leadership dans un environnement stimulant et collaboratif.
 Nous favorisons l'apprentissage continu, l'inclusion, le développement professionnel et le travail d'équipe afin de permettre à chacun de réaliser son plein potentiel et de contribuer à l'amélioration de la santé des patients.
 Comment postuler 
 Nous aimerions faire votre connaissance. Veuillez soumettre votre curriculum vitæ accompagné d'un court texte décrivant une situation où vous avez dirigé une amélioration technique, opérationnelle ou organisationnelle ayant eu un impact mesurable sur la qualité, la performance ou la conformité d'un procédé ou d'une équipe.
 Postulez dès maintenant pour contribuer à l'innovation technologique, à l'excellence opérationnelle et au succès de nos équipes.
 Compétences 
CMC Strategy, Data-Driven Decision Making, Data Integrity, Debate Moderation, Digital Fluency, GxP Regulations, Lean Management, Problem Solving, Process Optimization, Project Leadership, Risk Awareness, Scientific Writing, Technology Transfer  
 Pourquoi GSK?
Allier science, technologie et talent pour vaincre ensemble la maladie. 
 GSK est une entreprise biopharmaceutique mondiale dont la mission est de réunir la science, la technologie et le talent pour prendre ensemble de l'avance sur les maladies. Nous visons à avoir un impact positif sur la santé de 2,5 milliards de personnes d'ici la fin de la décennie, en tant qu'entreprise prospère et en croissance où les gens peuvent s'épanouir. Nous prenons de l'avance sur les maladies en les prévenant et en les traitant grâce à l'innovation dans les médicaments spécialisés et les vaccins. Nous nous concentrons sur quatre domaines thérapeutiques : les maladies respiratoires, l'immunologie et l'inflammation; l'oncologie; le VIH; les maladies infectieuses – pour avoir un impact à grande échelle sur la santé.
 Les gens et les patients partout dans le monde comptent sur les médicaments et les vaccins que nous produisons; c'est pourquoi nous nous engageons à créer un environnement où nos employés peuvent s'épanouir et se concentrer sur ce qui compte le plus. Notre culture, qui repose sur l'ambition pour les patients, la responsabilité de la portée et le fait de faire ce qui est juste, constitue la base de la manière dont nous tenons nos engagements ensemble pour les patients, les actionnaires et nos employés.
 GSK est un employeur offrant l'égalité des chances. Cela garantit que tous les candidats qualifiés recevront une considération égale pour l'emploi sans distinction de race, de couleur, de religion, de sexe (y compris la grossesse, l'identité de genre et l'orientation sexuelle), de statut parental, d'origine nationale, d'âge, de handicap, d'informations génétiques (y compris les antécédents médicaux familiaux), de service militaire ou de toute autre base interdite par la loi fédérale, étatique ou locale. GSK s'engage à accueillir les personnes handicapées. Si vous avez besoin d'un aménagement à n'importe quelle étape du processus de candidature ou si vous souhaitez plus d'informations sur nos politiques d'aménagement, veuillez nous contacter à canada-recruitment@gsk.com . Veuillez ne pas envoyer de CV à cette adresse e-mail et postuler plutôt via le processus de candidature en ligne de cette annonce.
 Avis important destiné aux services/agences de placement 
 GSK n’accepte pas les propositions des services/agences de placement en vue de pourvoir les postes affichés dans le présent site. Ces services/agences doivent s’adresser au service d’approvisionnement/des ressources humaines de GSK pour obtenir une autorisation écrite avant de lui proposer des candidats. Cette autorisation est une condition préalable à toute entente (orale ou écrite) entre le service/l’agence de placement et GSK. Sans cette autorisation écrite, toute mesure de la part du service/de l’agence de placement doit être considérée comme avoir été appliquée sans le consentement ni l’entente contractuelle de GSK. Par conséquent, GSK ne peut pas être tenue responsable des honoraires attribuables à de telles mesures ni à quelque recommandation que ce soit de la part du service/de l’agence de placement en ce qui concerne sa proposition de candidature en vue de pouvoir un poste annoncé dans le présent site.

About Behavox: 
 Behavox is shaping the future for how businesses harness their most important raw material - data. Our mission is bold: Organize enterprise data into actionable information that protects and promotes the business growth of multinational companies around the world. 
 From managing enterprise risk and compliance to maximizing revenue and value, our data operating platform presents a widespread opportunity to build multilingual, AI/ML-based solutions that activate data for every function within a global enterprise. 
 Our approach is unique, and it’s validated by our customers who tell us to keep forging ahead because no one else is aggregating, analyzing, and acting on data to uncover opportunities or solve problems quite the way we are. 
 We are looking for fearless innovators who have an insatiable appetite for building what no one has built before. 
 This is a hybrid role with 1 day in the office. 
 About the Role: 
 The Senior HR Business Partner is an individual contributor responsible for partnering with US and Canada business leaders to execute people strategies that support organizational performance and growth. 
 The role applies strong business acumen and HR expertise to advise leaders on workforce planning, performance management, employee relations, and organizational effectiveness within the US and Canada client group, and covers this territory directly and in full. 
 Reporting to the Principal HR Business Partner, the Senior HR Business Partner partners with leaders to deliver people initiatives while ensuring alignment with global frameworks and applicable US and Canada employment requirements. 
 During the initial phase of the role, the Senior HR Business Partner works under close coaching from the Principal HR Business Partner while building full ownership of the client group; oversight reduces as competence across the remit is demonstrated. 
 The role supports workforce planning, organizational design, and post-merger workforce integration workstreams for its client group, executes assigned enterprise HR programs and projects, and independently manages moderate-to-complex employee relations matters, escalating matters of significant complexity, cross-jurisdictional exposure, or elevated organizational risk to the Principal HR Business Partner. 
 It uses workforce data and people metrics to inform recommendations for its client group, and may be asked to support the Principal HR Business Partner on workforce matters outside the US and Canada as the function's footprint grows. 
 What You'll Bring: 
 HR Business Partnering — Applies working knowledge of business priorities and workforce needs within the US and Canada client group to align people initiatives with business objectives and provide trusted advisory support to leaders and managers at all levels. 
 Workforce Planning and Organizational Support — Applies workforce planning methodologies and organizational design principles to support headcount planning, org changes, and business effectiveness within the client group, in line with the framework set by the Principal HR Business Partner. 
 Employment Law and Employee Relations (US & Canada) — Maintains working knowledge of US and Canadian employment legislation and regulatory frameworks, independently managing moderate-to-complex employee relations matters within those jurisdictions. Working knowledge of employment fundamentals in other jurisdictions (e.g., UK, EMEA, APAC) is desirable, as the role may be asked to support the wider HR Business Partner team outside its core territory. 
 Talent Management and Performance — Applies performance management, career development, and talent process knowledge to support capability development within the client group. 
 People Analytics — Uses workforce metrics, organizational data, and HRIS-derived reporting to evaluate trends and support evidence-based decisions within the client group. 
 What You'll Do: 
 HR Advisory — Provides sound, commercially informed HR guidance to leaders on moderate-to-complex workforce and talent challenges within the US and Canada client group, exercising judgment on approach and escalating matters that exceed this level's scope. 
 Employee Relations Case Management — Manages moderate-to-complex employee relations cases end-to-end within US and Canada employment frameworks, balancing legal compliance, business priorities, and employee experience. 
 People Program Delivery — Delivers and locally adapts HR programs (performance cycles, workforce planning inputs, career development processes) for the client group in line with enterprise standards. 
 Workforce Data Interpretation — Interprets workforce data and people metrics for the client group to identify trends and inform recommendations to leaders, including through periods of increased organizational scrutiny or governance rigor (e.g., audit readiness, compliance program maturation, or a prior employer's scale-up or pre-exit period). 
 Compensation Analysis — Applies compensation data and benchmarking to support pay recommendations, offer construction, and pay equity considerations for the client group, escalating matters requiring Principal-level or Total Rewards review. 
 What We Offer 
 The opportunity to work on a global, mission-critical AI platform alongside the best engineers and technologists across multiple geographies 
 A role with real ownership and impact, building complex systems at scale in an environment that values speed, experimentation, and technical excellence 
 A highly attractive benefits package, including competitive cash compensation, an equity award aligned with long-term value creation, and comprehensive health insurance for employees and their families 
 Modern, comfortable offices in Montreal/Toronto downtown, with an expectation of (hybrid) working from the office 1 day per week, reflecting our belief in strong in-person collaboration. 
 A generous time-off policy of 30 days annually, plus public holidays and sick leave, recognizing the importance of sustained high performance 
 About Our Process 
 We take Talent very seriously and we are building a community of extraordinary individuals working together in very high performing teams. We also know that the best Talent always has options so we believe that the process has to be a two way assessment - the company AND the candidate assessing the business needs alignment, the career next step alignment, and the cultural alignment. 
 During the process we will begin by exploring the core factors regarding salary and location along with core experience and skills and values alignment. We will then deep dive explore the critical technical competencies we have identified for the role, and then we will deep dive in behavioral competencies. 
 The most aligned candidate will then be asked to do a practical work task simulation activity so we can make sure that you will enjoy the kind of work the role requires, and this task will typically be presented and discussed with a group of colleagues and managers. Finally we will ask you to meet with a number of our senior leaders to make sure that you are making the most informed call possible. 
 Please note that: 
 We want to get to know you and have a genuine conversation, so the use of AI tools or assistance during live interviews is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate disqualification from the process. 
 Interviews may be recorded for internal review purposes to ensure fairness and enable collaborative hiring discussions within the team.

About Owner

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.



Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.



Our vision



We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.



But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.



Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.



In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.



Our traction



Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com http://Owner.com website.



More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.



Our team



Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.



We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.



Where we work



Owner is a remote-first, global company headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto. For a few of our roles we prioritize in-person collaboration at one of our office locations. Most of our teammates are distributed throughout the globe. Please review the role description and discuss with your recruiter for more details on location!





Role Overview

Owner is the leading all-in-one platform for independent restaurants, and 2026 is the year we engineer a true product-led growth motion: restaurant owners should be able to go from discovering Owner all the way to running their whole business on it, opting into each next step because they trust it's worth it.

As we scale that motion, we're expanding our product engineering leadership to accelerate our ability to ship fast, delight restaurant owners, and build infrastructure that scales with us. As an Engineering Manager for Launch and Websites, you'll lead teams of fullstack engineers building the core product surfaces owners rely on every day - from the self-serve launch journey that takes them from Grader to POS, to the website design, builder, and generation systems that put their brand online. This role is equal parts product intuition and technical execution. You'll be trusted to make fast, high-quality decisions, ship impactful features, and grow a team that embodies engineering excellence.

We move with urgency, bias toward simplicity, and expect our leaders to be hands-on when needed. If you're energized by ownership, decisive execution, and solving real problems for small business owners, we'd love to hear from you.



Why we’re looking for you

Today, most restaurant owners lose an enormous amount of time and trust just getting live on Owner and getting a website that actually represents their brand, instead of running their business. Launch owns the self-serve journey that takes an owner from Grader all the way to POS - engineering the automation and trust signals that let owners opt into each next step without needing a person to walk them through it. Websites owns the design, builder, and AI-powered generation systems that put a restaurant's brand online, closing the customization gaps that drive churn and increasing the number of high-quality sites we launch.

These two teams sit at the center of Owner's product-led growth motion this year - systems directly in the critical path for how independent restaurants activate, launch, and show up online.

We're looking for an Engineering Manager who cares deeply about the craft and the team behind it - someone who's led full-stack engineers building customer-facing product end-to-end, and who's excited to build a strong, durable engineering culture across two of our most strategically important product areas.



Our Stack

 - Frontend: React, Next.js, TypeScript

 - Backend: Node.js, TypeScript

 - Databases: MongoDB, PostgreSQL

 - Infrastructure & Observability: Temporal, Datadog, AWS

 - TypeScript everywhere



What we’re looking for

 - ~3 years of experience in a software engineering management role leading fullstack product engineering teams, preferably in high-growth environments

 - A track record of leading high-performing, engaged full-stack engineering teams - not purely backend-platform or purely frontend teams

 - Strong product sense and an instinct for balancing speed, quality, and user impact

 - Experience with modern frontend frameworks (e.g. React) and backend systems (e.g. Node.js)

 - High degree of cross-functional collaboration - past colleagues in product, design, and business would speak highly of your teamwork

 - A plus: growth or PLG experience (self-serve activation, onboarding, upgrade flows) - desirable, not required

 - A plus: experience applying LLMs or agents (research, enrichment, next-best-action, automated diagnosis)



Compensation and benefits

 - The estimated base salary range for this role is $230K-$250K, depending on experience and location. The offer also includes a a generous pre-IPO equity package.

 - Other benefits include comprehensive health coverage, remote-first workplace, unlimited PTO - plus extra fun perks!





Notice - Employment Scams

Communication from our team regarding job opportunities will only be made by an Owner team member with an @owner.com email address.



We do not conduct interviews over email or chat platforms, and we will never ask you to provide personal or financial information such as your mailing address, social security number, credit card numbers or banking information. If you believe you are being contacted by a scammer, please mark the communication as "phishing" or “spam” and do not respond.

We have recently become part of the Securitas group, and we are looking for a Talent Acquisition Partner to own hiring and the employee lifecycle as we scale.  Reporting to the Director, People & Culture and working alongside our People Operations Specialist, you will be Liferaft’s dedicated talent acquisition expert, owning hiring across GTM, Engineering, Product & Innovation, and G&A. Your mandate is clear: bring exceptional people into Liferaft who continually raise the talent bar and the organizational capabilities. 
 Talent acquisition is at the core of this role, but your impact goes further. As part of a small People & Culture team, you will also own key areas of the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, learning and development, recognition and retention. This is a builder implementer role with real autonomy to turn ideas into programs, processes and outcomes. 
 What you do as the Talent Acquisition Partner at Liferaft 
 Full Cycle Talent Acquisition 
 Own recruitment across all functions, from intake and role scoping through sourcing, assessment, offer and close.
 Set clear criteria, structured interviews and scorecards with hiring managers. Hold the bar through every search and push back on slates that fall short.
 Build proactive pipelines and stay current on competitor hiring, talent availability and compensation. Use that data to shape workforce planning, role requirements and hiring decisions.
 Own Workable administration, reporting, templates and candidate data. Track recruitment metrics and hiring plan attainment, and keep the candidate experience consistent from first contact to final follow up.
 Manage recruitment vendors, job boards and search firms, and coordinate background checks and offer documentation with People Operations.
 Support internal career ladders and keep job descriptions levelled against Pave, Mercer and Securitas job architecture.
 AI Enabled Recruitment and Lifecycle 
 Build and run AI workflows for sourcing, screening, interviewing, market research and pipeline analysis, cutting admin without cutting quality, consistency or fairness.

 Own onboarding from offer through 30, 60 and 90 day plans, including manager readiness, and improve it based on new hire feedback.
 Build and maintain an onboarding program and knowledge base covering our platform, customers, industry and competitors, working with internal experts to create the content.
 Run a quarterly learning program that deepens industry and market knowledge. Coordinate the experts, facilitate the sessions and improve them based on feedback.
 Own exit interviews and offboarding, and partner with People Operations to spot departure trends and address what is driving them.
 Retention, Recognition and Employer Brand 
 Own recognition programs within budget, including peer recognition, quarterly awards and spot bonuses, and run the employee referral program.
 Help managers spot and act on retention risks. Support eNPS and pulse surveys and own the follow up actions.
 Own Liferaft’s employer brand and careers content.
 What You Need to Get the Job Done
 Experience 
 5+ years of full cycle recruitment, with at least 3 in B2B SaaS , ideally through a scaling stage.
 Experience as a sole or lead recruiter with no coordinator or sourcer support, delivering 20+ quality hires a year across functions.
 Technical hiring across engineering, data, AI/ML, product and design, plus enterprise GTM hiring across account executives, sales engineers and customer success.
 Hands on ATS administration (Workable an asset) and real examples of using AI to improve recruitment or people operations results.
 Experience owning onboarding, offboarding or other lifecycle programs alongside recruitment. You want a role that goes beyond TA.
 Knowledge of hiring, offer, candidate data and recordkeeping requirements in Nova Scotia, Ontario and Quebec, and experience recruiting in specialized markets with small candidate pools.
 Skills and Attributes 
 Excellence only. You would rather leave a role open than fill it with the wrong person, and you can make that case to a hiring manager.
 Highly autonomous. You set priorities and act without waiting for direction.
 Always learning. You keep your own skills sharp, stay current on sourcing methods, AI tools and the SaaS talent market, and bring what you learn back to the team.
 Credible with the business. You understand functions, markets and roles, and you challenge scope, levels, process and compensation without damaging the relationship.
 Organized and clear. You write well and can run several searches and lifecycle priorities at once without dropping quality or responsiveness.
 Credible in front of a room. You can facilitate a session for the whole company on a topic where someone else is the expert, keep it on time, and keep it useful.
 CPHR designation or a recruitment certification is an asset.
 How Success Is Measured 
 Quality of hire, hiring plan attainment, time to fill (improving from a first quarter baseline) and offer acceptance rate.
 New hire retention, source effectiveness and cost per hire, including less reliance on agencies and retained search.
 Onboarding and offboarding done to standard, learning delivered on schedule with new hires understanding our platform, customers and market within 90 days, and measurable time saved through AI.

 Autonomy. We don’t hire the best of the best just to micro-manage them

 Full health and dental package covered at 80% by the employer, with $3000/annum mental health coverage

 Annual lifestyle subsidy

About Burq
 We're revolutionizing commerce from port to doorstep with Burq Intelligence.
 Burq started with an ambitious mission: to turn the complex process of offering delivery into a simple, turnkey solution. It's a big mission, and now we want you to join us in making it even bigger.
 We're proud to be recognized as one of Fast Company's Best Workplaces for Innovators and a 2025 Inc. Magazine Power Partner, awards that highlight how we're redefining the future of logistics while empowering our partners to grow.
 Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors like Village Global, the fund whose investors include Bill Gates, Jeff Bezos, Mark Zuckerberg, Reid Hoffman, and Sara Blakely, we've built a world-class team across the globe.
 We operate at scale but remain small enough for every person to have a massive impact. There's a lot of important work ahead, and joining Burq means the opportunity to grow faster than ever while doing the most meaningful work of your career.
 The role
 We're hiring a Staff ML/OR engineer to define and build the intelligence at the core of Dispatch OS, our platform for ML-assisted dispatch decisions. You'll set the technical direction for how Burq prices, selects, forecasts, and routes deliveries, and you'll personally build the highest-leverage models and optimization systems behind it.
 You'll own the architecture and roadmap for ML and optimization across the platform, make the key technical bets, and raise the bar for how we build, evaluate, and ship models. This is a hands-on IC role with company-level impact on revenue, margin, and delivery reliability.
 What you'll do
 Technical leadership
 Technical direction: own the ML and optimization roadmap for Dispatch OS, deciding which problems get ML, which get solvers, which stay heuristic, and in what order
 Architecture: design the end-to-end architecture for model serving, evaluation, and optimization so it scales with order volume, new providers, and new customers
 Hardest problems: lead the most ambiguous, high-stakes modeling and optimization problems from framing through production, and guide technical work across Engineering and Data
 Raise the bar: set standards for experimentation, evaluation, and production ML, and mentor engineers through design reviews, pairing, and code review
 Strategic partnership: work with Product and leadership to shape product strategy and identify where ML and OR create competitive advantage
 Core systems
 Quote selection and pricing: design and ship models for quote selection, dynamic pricing, and reliability scoring that measurably improve margin, win rate, and conversion
 Forecasting: build demand and volume forecasting models, including modern deep learning approaches where they outperform classical methods, to - help operations and customers plan driver and fleet capacity
 Optimization: move dispatch decisions from heuristics to solver-based optimization for batching, route optimization, and vehicle/fleet recommendation, using OR-Tools, Gurobi, or similar where it earns its keep
 LLMs and agents: apply LLMs and AI agents to dispatch workflows, such as extracting provider rules and rate terms from documents, and automating quote follow-ups and exception handling
 Evaluation and trust: build rigorous, replayable evaluation frameworks that let customers verify a model's performance against their own historical decisions before they trust it to act
 Constraint translation: turn real operational constraints (driver availability, provider rules, cost ceilings) into model requirements, scoring logic, and optimization formulations
 MLOps: design and own automated pipelines for training, deployment, and monitoring so models stay accurate in production at scale
 AI-native work: use AI tools daily to speed up experimentation, automate eval pipelines, and debug faster
 Requirements
 9+ years in applied ML or ML engineering, including multiple years operating at the senior or staff level, with models shipped to and maintained in production
 Track record of setting technical direction for ML or optimization systems, where architecture decisions you made shaped a product or platform over multiple years
 Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical initiatives across teams without direct authority
 Track record of ML or optimization systems with quantified, company-level business impact (e.g., tens of millions in revenue, or major utilization or margin gains), ideally in pricing, logistics, marketplaces, or operations
 Deep experience with decision, ranking, and scoring problems where model outputs directly drive a business action
 Strong quantitative and algorithmic reasoning, including combinatorial problems, constraint satisfaction, and algorithm design
 Hands-on experience formulating and solving optimization problems (LP/MIP, constraint programming, or VRP-style routing)
 Experience with time-series forecasting in production
 Hands-on experience deploying LLM-based systems in production, such as fine-tuned models, extraction pipelines, or agents
 Experience owning end-to-end ML pipelines and MLOps (training, deployment, monitoring, retraining)
 Comfortable with messy, incomplete, constraint-heavy operational data, and able to build models that honor hard business constraints rather than treating them as soft penalties
 Experience building evaluation frameworks that non-technical stakeholders can understand and trust
 Nice to have
 Experience with delivery/dispatch software, TMS platforms, or routing systems
 Production experience with commercial or open-source solvers (OR-Tools, Gurobi, CPLEX)
 Pricing or revenue management experience in aviation, fleet, or transportation
 Published work, patents, or open-source contributions in ML, OR, or pricing
 Investing in you 🙏
 Fully remote
 Medical, vision, and dental insurance
 Reimbursement for educational courses
 Generous time off

Senior Support Engineer 
 Town Web · HeyGov · ClerkMinutes. Remote, Central US hours. $85,000 to $105,000 a year. Open to candidates in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland.
 About us 
 We make municipal software built for clerks: websites residents can use, forms and payments that replace stacks of paper, and meeting minutes drafted after every meeting. More than 1,300 local governments rely on us, from counties and cities to villages and towns. We have local government clients in almost every state in the U.S.
 Our clients are municipal clerks and the government teams around them. They keep city hall running and rarely get thanked for it. Your job is to make working with us the easy part of their week.
 The role 
 This is the senior seat on our Client Success team. We are hiring you to raise the standard of our support: fix what is broken, write down how it should work, and show what great looks like.
 Our AI agent now answers repeatable, well-documented questions. What is left is the work that only a person can do: own a client's problem from the first message to the confirmed fix, build a relationship a clerk trusts, and turn what you learn into better documentation and a better product.
 This is not a ticket-closing job. Think of a great 5-star hotel that puts slippers by the bed before you ask. We want a clerk to finish a conversation with you and tell the clerk in the next town about the great experience they had. If that takes three calls, take three calls.
 It is also a technical job. You will work with our developers every day. When something breaks, you work out where it lives before anyone else has to. Is the problem on the events calendar on the client's homepage, or in the calendar widget embedded on a department page? Is the wrong speaker name only in the transcript, or is it also in the finished minutes? You reproduce it, write it up so a developer can act without a follow-up question, stay on it until it ships, and tell the client yourself.
 You need both halves. A brilliant troubleshooter who is short with a clerk will not work here. Neither will a lovely person who forwards every problem to a developer.
 Your first 90 days 
 Learn all of our products well enough to teach them
 Take over every open escalation and close or schedule each one
 Rebuild the path from support to our developers so nothing leaves the queue untracked
 Find the ten questions clerks ask most and fix each at the source: an article, a Fin answer, or a product change
 What you will do 
 Raise the standard 
 Design how issues move from support to developers, and keep that path working
 Set the bar for replies, calls, and write-ups, and coach teammates by example
 Turn what you fix into playbooks the team and Fin can follow
 Delight clients 
 Make every interaction feel personal, warm, and unhurried, especially for less technical users who would rather talk to a person than read a help article
 Step in when the AI agent or the documentation is not enough, and make sure the client feels heard and helped, not processed
 Treat client sentiment as the real measure of success, not ticket speed
 Look for small moments to go above and beyond, and share what works so it becomes how the whole team operates
 Own the problem from start to finish 
 Be the named person on an account when things go wrong: one owner, one plan, regular updates, until the client says it is fixed
 Step in early when an account shows strain (repeat tickets, a rough launch, a frustrated message) and run the recovery. Get on a call, write down what is open, set dates, follow through
 Make sure nothing sits untracked once it leaves the support queue
 Diagnose, then escalate 
 Work out which product and which layer an issue lives in before you hand it to a developer
 Reproduce it, capture the steps with screenshots or a recording, and file it in Linear with everything a developer needs
 Check on your open Linear issues, chase what is stuck, and confirm the fix with the client
 Use Claude, connected to our code repository, to trace where a behavior comes from. For small, well-understood fixes, draft the change for a developer to review
 Knowledge base and AI support 
 Inherit and maintain the help center for all of our products. It is what our AI agent (Fin, in Intercom) answers from
 Write and improve articles from real, recurring questions, on a weekly rhythm measured against live ticket volume
 Write troubleshooting guides that separate look-alike problems, so the next person, or Fin, can tell them apart
 Tune Fin: review where it failed, fix the article, and teach it to ask a clarifying question when a request could mean two things
 Record short training videos so clients can learn at their own pace
 Support and onboarding 
 Handle the conversations Fin cannot resolve across Town Web (websites), HeyGov (forms, payments, reservations, campaigns), and ClerkMinutes (agendas, transcripts, minutes)
 Help new clients through onboarding with the projects team so they reach value quickly
 Talk with clerks by phone and video every week. Get on a call whenever a situation needs a human voice
 Account care 
 Build real relationships with your assigned accounts
 Understand what each client is trying to accomplish, what they use, what they do not know we offer, and where they will need help before they ask
 Run proactive, recurring check-ins instead of waiting for tickets. For example, reach out a few weeks after go-live to review how their forms are performing
 Use product usage data to spot clients who are not getting full value yet
 Meet clients in person. Join us at clerk conferences and marketing events a few times a year. We cover all travel & lodging expenses
 Spot opportunity 
 Tell clients about services they do not use yet (digital forms, payments, .gov domains, accessibility, training) without it feeling like a pitch
 Flag possible expansion and renewal opportunities to the sales team
 Training 
 Get clients to real proficiency with the product, not just past their immediate question
 Work with Product Managers to co-host webinars about new features and training
 Tools you will use: Intercom and Fin, Linear, Claude, our help center, screen recording, Zoom phone.
 How we work 
 Delight over deflection. The goal is happy, successful clients, not fewer conversations
 Ownership over routing. A hard case is yours until it is resolved
 Diagnose before you escalate. A developer should never have to ask what the client actually saw
 Documentation is the foundation everything else runs on, not an afterthought
 Teaching over ticket-closing. Proficiency, not just an answer
 Who you are 
 You like people, and it shows. Clerks are often not technical, sometimes stressed, and now and then upset. You pick up the phone gladly and leave them calmer than you found them
 Hospitable by nature. A background in hospitality or another service-first field is a plus
 You have done support somewhere known for it. The standard we have in mind is Basecamp: competent, calm, and trusted to make the call
 Technically deep. You read the error, open the browser console and the network tab, check a DNS record, find your way around WordPress, and follow the trail into the code with Claude's help
 At home with developers. You know what a good bug report contains and you have filed plenty
 High autonomy. You decide, act, and report. You do not wait to be told
 A clear, warm, precise writer, with clients and across teams
 A natural teacher, patient with less technical users
 Able to see the whole account, not just the ticket in front of you
 Who you might be
 Someone who worked the Genius Bar at an Apple Store and misses solving problems for a person, not a queue
 Someone who learned support at a company known for it, such as Basecamp, Automattic, or Help Scout
 A hotel or hospitality professional who moved into software and kept the instincts
 A former municipal or deputy clerk who was always the one who figured out the software. You already know our clients' world
 Or maybe none of these! If the rest of this page sounds like you, we certainly want to hear from you
 This is not the job for you if 
 You would rather work a queue than talk to people
 You find non-technical users frustrating
 You want to hand a problem to a developer and move on
 You need someone to tell you what to do next
 Work style 
 Independent and ownership-driven. You do not need heavy oversight to perform
 Comfortable wearing several hats across products and brands
 Comfortable in a lean, documentation-first team
 Proactive rather than reactive with accounts
 What success looks like 
 Clients describe working with us as a great experience
 No client has to ask who is handling their problem. They already know it is you
 Issues you file get fixed without a developer asking for more detail
 Tickets stop recurring, not just get answered
 Help center articles created or improved every week, and Fin resolving more each month
 Repeat questions turned into product fixes or automation
 Expansion and renewals tied to the accounts you touch
 Account relationships that are trusted, not just responsive
 The rest of the team gets better because you are on it
 Experience 
 Five or more years in technical support or support engineering at a software company, working directly with engineers
 An issue tracker used daily: Linear preferred, Jira or similar is fine
 Intercom or similar support tooling, including work with an AI support agent
 A knowledge base you wrote that other people relied on
 AI tools such as Claude already part of your daily work
 Nice to have: government or municipal software, WordPress-based websites, hospitality or other service-first work
 Able to travel within the US a few times a year. Not required, but very helpful to understand our customers better.
 How to apply 
 Apply through Workable. You will answer two short questions in writing and record a two-minute Loom video teaching us one thing
 Complete the Culture Index survey. You can do it right after you apply. We only review candidates who have completed it
 Interview with our Head of Client Success
 Paid take-home exercise built from real client situations
 Conversation with our CTO and founder, including a short role-play call with a clerk who needs help
 Offer letter, if selected
 Salary of $85,000 to $105,000 a year, depending on experience
 20 paid vacation days, plus public holidays for your country of residence
 Fully remote, working Central US hours
 Internet stipend
 Gym membership or wellness stipend
 We do not offer a health plan or a 401(k) today. The salary range reflects that.

10 places are open for the 2027 term, with a duration of 6 or 12 months at the applicant's option.
 Purpose 
 There is a crisis in academic AI/ML research. What is still worth working on?
 Paper submissions have doubled on the arXiv and at ML conferences, and yet many submitters cannot even answer questions about the details of "their" work.
 Many people across applied research and theory groups, whether math, physics, or computer science, have the distinct feeling that perhaps it is pointless to work on anything other than AI safety and continual learning.
 If we simply draw a line continuing the capabilities progress of the past two years forward, it seems possible that human contributions will be a marginal input in many areas of research within two or three years.
 At the same time, it is clear that fundamental questions in model architecture, sample efficiency, explainability, and creativity are still unanswered, and that making progress on these topics is very likely to benefit humanity over the next two years.
 Designing or training for explainability and determinism may be much easier than achieving post hoc understanding of circuits forced out of scaled data by gradient descent and optimized through blind RL.
 Our focus instead is on frontier research: order-of-magnitude improvements, rather than disposable papers barely better than baseline. 
 The intent of these fellowships is to give awardees uninterrupted time to focus on harder open problems, with adequate compute, talented peers, and weekly 1:1 mentorship from senior researchers but without chasing specific metrics.
 You will be expected to spend about 80% of your time on your own research, and up to 20% of your time either assisting other fellows or participating in wider research programs at IMI.
 We focus largely on applied research and its applications to online security problems, but often publish and support frontier research aligned with our broader interests. Serving hundreds of millions of people gives us a unique perspective as to what works at scale.
 Eligibility:  previous fellows and research staff have come from disparate backgrounds, including early career researchers previously at MSR, FAIR, Mila, MPI, etc. and self taught senior engineers transitioning into research.
 We do not discriminate on the basis of pedigree or age. If you have done interesting work, that is enough.
 Conversely, if you don't already have publications that show you can do good self-directed research then this is not the right opportunity.
 Do not apply if you have no public evidence that you can do good self-directed research and produce results. 
 Location:  you may reside anywhere in the world, excluding sanctioned jurisdictions. This will be a remote fellowship. We do not sponsor visas.
 Deliverables:  we do not have hard targets, and focus on quality. Fellows generally get 1-2 papers with code done in a year, targeting NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, etc. At the end of your fellowship, if the threshold for refereed publication is unmet we will expect a final report, which may be published as a blog post.
 Full details are available at: https://www.imachines.com/imi-ai-ml-fellowships-2025-2026-high-risk-research 
 (imachines dot com slash imi-ai-ml-fellowships-2025-2026-high-risk-research)
 Please note that if you are unable to find this page on our website you will be unable to correctly answer the questions required to submit an application, and your application will be automatically discarded.
 Applying:  send a brief bio / CV link via this page. Include 1) the topic you are interested in working on, 2) a few lines on any relevant prior work you've done, 3) your github / scholar / x links, 4) your desired start date, duration, and other obligations (if any) during that period, and 5) a brief analysis of one of the projects outlined on the page linked above.
 Each project we have listed intentionally includes some gaps or glosses. List the ones you see, and how you'd solve them. Alternatively, if you dislike the projects outlined under a particular topic, briefly write up your own idea and why it is more promising, along with your estimate of time and compute required.
 Deadline:  Admitting fellows in two cohorts. Deadlines for consideration: April 1 and September 1 2026. 3 week decision period. Rolling thereafter.
 Compensation:  competitive location-adjusted stipend, conference and travel support for conferences with accepted papers.
 After the fellowship:  past fellows have stayed on in full-time roles at IMI or co-founded AI unicorns. This is a selective process, so we claim little credit for their success. However, we will support your next steps.
 Selection criteria:  novelty and importance, clarity of approach, feasibility given time/compute, alignment with topics. Panel review and one interview.
 Using AI: Coding agents are useful tools. We provide access to the top models, and were early adopters of evals-first development flows.
 Familiarity with coding using agents is part of all interviews. However, reliability and correctness are critical for us. You will need to read and understand every line of code with your name on it, and it will be reviewed by both people and machines.
 Selection is based on merit. We promote equality of opportunity, and welcome applications from anyone with talent, skills and potential. IMI is an equal opportunity employer, and does not discriminate on the basis of age, disability, sex, orientation, race, religion or belief. 
 Please note that all positions require pre-employment screening, including third-party verification of work history, education, and identity, as well as a final in-person interview and identity verification step, which will be conducted in your country of residence.

We are looking for a Self-Driving Systems Specialist (SDS Specialist) to support the diagnostics, calibration, configuration, and technical readiness of self-driving systems used in autonomous vehicles and robotaxi fleets across North America.
The SDS Specialist focuses on the technology layer of autonomous mobility: sensors, compute systems, software configurations, autonomous driving hardware, system diagnostics, calibration procedures, and technical validation. This role ensures that the self-driving system installed in each autonomous vehicle is functioning correctly, accurately calibrated, and ready to support safe testing, commercial deployment, and autonomous ride-hailing operations.
You will work closely with Senior Technicians, AV Operations Leads, Safety Operators, Depot Specialists, engineering teams, and fleet operations teams to identify technical issues, execute structured troubleshooting procedures, and support reliable operation of autonomous vehicle platforms.
This position is ideal for candidates with experience in automotive electronics, ADAS systems, embedded systems, robotics, diagnostics, calibration, or complex technical support who want to work at the center of autonomous vehicle deployment and robotaxi operations.

Key Responsibilities: Self-Driving System Diagnostics 
 Diagnose and troubleshoot self-driving system issues affecting autonomous vehicle performance and fleet readiness.
 Investigate technical problems related to cameras, LiDAR, radar, GPS/GNSS, compute units, sensors, connectivity modules, wiring, and autonomous driving hardware.
 Execute structured diagnostic procedures to identify root causes of SDS hardware, software, and configuration issues.
 Support advanced troubleshooting for autonomous vehicle faults that impact testing, commercial operations, or robotaxi fleet availability .
 Escalate complex technical cases to engineering teams with clear findings and supporting documentation.
 Hardware Support 
 Inspect, repair, replace, and validate SDS hardware components installed on autonomous vehicles.
 Support installation and verification of cameras, LiDAR units, radar sensors, compute hardware, sensor mounts, antennas, and related components.
 Confirm that autonomous driving hardware is correctly installed, secured, clean, functional, and ready for operation.
 Collaborate with Senior Technicians on vehicle-level issues involving both standard automotive systems and SDS components.
 Ensure all hardware work is completed according to strict safety, quality, and technical procedures.
 Software Configuration & Updates 
 Perform software updates, configuration changes, and system validation checks for autonomous driving systems.
 Execute defined software procedures using diagnostic tools, command-line tools, configuration files, or engineering-provided workflows.
 Verify successful software installation and confirm that the SDS is operational before the vehicle returns to service.
 Support troubleshooting of software-related issues affecting autonomous vehicle behavior, system communication, or operational readiness.
 Maintain accurate records of software versions, configurations, updates, and validation results.
 Sensor Calibration & Validation 
 Perform calibration and verification activities for autonomous vehicle sensors and self-driving system components.
 Support calibration workflows involving cameras, LiDAR, radar, localization systems, and other perception-related hardware.
 Validate that the self-driving system is functioning correctly after maintenance, software updates, hardware replacement, or vehicle service.
 Assist engineering teams with data collection, calibration testing, and system performance verification.
 Ensure autonomous vehicles meet technical readiness requirements before returning to robotaxi operations or on-road testing.
 Engineering & Operations Support 
 Serve as the on-site subject matter expert for SDS-related technical issues.
 Provide structured technical findings to engineering, fleet operations, and project teams.
 Collaborate with AV Operations Leads to prioritize SDS-related repairs and reduce vehicle downtime.
 Support incident reviews, root-cause analysis, and technical escalation processes.
 Contribute to continuous improvement of troubleshooting workflows, calibration procedures, and operational documentation.
 Documentation & Compliance 
 Maintain accurate records of diagnostics, repairs, software updates, hardware changes, and calibration activities.
 Follow strict operational, safety, and technical procedures when working with autonomous driving systems.
 Complete all required system validation checklists and technical reports.
 Support compliance with internal quality standards, safety protocols, and customer requirements.
 Ensure all SDS-related work is traceable, repeatable, and properly documented.
Requirements: Essential 
 Minimum 3+ years of experience in automotive electronics, diagnostics, embedded systems, robotics, technical support, or complex technical systems.
 Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills.
 Experience working with vehicle electronics, sensors, control systems, or advanced technical hardware.
 Comfortable following structured software procedures and technical workflows.
 Ability to work with diagnostic tools, logs, technical documentation, and engineering instructions.
 High attention to detail and strong procedural discipline.
 Good communication skills and ability to work with cross-functional technical teams.
 Fluent English.
 Strongly Preferred 
 Experience with ADAS , autonomous vehicles, robotics, sensor systems, or advanced driver assistance technologies.
 Familiarity with LiDAR, radar, camera systems, GNSS, IMU, compute units, or perception-related hardware.
 Experience with Linux, command-line tools, CAN bus, vehicle networks, or embedded systems.
 Experience performing calibration, validation, or system integration activities.
 Background in automotive testing, AV operations, robotics labs, fleet diagnostics, or technical field support.
What We Are Looking For: Successful SDS Specialists are precise, structured, and technically curious. They enjoy solving complex system problems and understand that reliable self-driving system performance is essential for safe autonomous vehicle operations , commercial robotaxi services , and fleet scaling.
 This role requires someone who can work carefully with advanced hardware and software, follow engineering procedures exactly, and communicate findings clearly to both technical and operational teams. You should be comfortable working in a depot or technical operations environment where autonomous vehicles must be diagnosed, validated, and returned to service quickly and safely.
What We Offer: Opportunity to work directly with self-driving systems , autonomous driving hardware, and advanced vehicle technologies.
 Hands-on involvement in robotaxi fleet operations , autonomous vehicle testing , and autonomous ride-hailing deployment across North America.
 Exposure to robotics, ADAS, sensor calibration, embedded systems, EV platforms, and next-generation mobility technologies.
 Structured onboarding, technical procedures, and ongoing training.
 Career development opportunities in autonomous vehicle operations, AV diagnostics, robotics, and technical fleet support.
 Collaboration with engineering, operations, depot, technician, and safety teams.
 Opportunity to support new city launches , fleet scaling, and commercial autonomous mobility programs.
